summary: The candidate coalesces touching ranges and removes the reported shared-page assertion, but its allocator-wide last-call fingerprint only suppresses consecutive retries. An A, B, A cleanup sequence frees A's pages twice, so cleanup remains non-idempotent under the approved interleaved-retry contract.

tests.what_was_measured: The actual base free_kv_row_segments path raised AssertionError: segment at 5 shares a page with the one ending at 5 for touching [0,5) and [5,7) ranges.

tests.command: PYTHONPATH=/job/repo/python /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-836f53935809/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q <five exact candidate regression nodeids>
tests.what_was_measured: All five candidate regressions passed (5 passed), covering touching coalescing and immediate retries in paged, SWA, and unified SWA allocators.
Touching cleanup freed two pages and an immediate retry freed zero more; interleaved A, B, A cleanup produced deltas 2, 1, 2 instead of 2, 1, 0.
The same result was observed with allocator tensors on the assigned AMD Instinct MI350X: the original touching case passed, but interleaved retry A freed two duplicate pages.

gpu_evidence: PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 reported one AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950), and the adversarial allocator probe ran with device=cuda:0.
remaining_counterexamples: With one allocator, free row A, then row B, then retry the identical segments for A. The candidate overwrites _last_kv_row_free while freeing B, so retry A inserts A's two physical pages into free_pages again (observed total growth 5 pages where 3 unique pages were released).
remaining_limitations: The production configuration uses 8 NVIDIA B300 GPUs (SM103), while the prepared host provides one AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) under ROCm 7.2; the full Kimi-K3 multi-rank abort workload was not reproducible here.
No model weights or eight-GPU topology were available. Validation therefore exercised the actual free_kv_row_segments and allocator paths directly, on CPU and the assigned GPU.

The candidate changes Python only. repository-environment.json declares native=null and wheel=null, so no native rebuild was applicable; imports were confirmed from /job/repo/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/common.py.
